title: An admitted mistake may still unsettle
meaning: You can discover a remark’s mistaken basis and share an understanding of the misunderstanding, acknowledging how losing certainty can unsettle you after a clear correction.
text: On your Vishuddha, the Tower in the physical position appears when a remark’s mistaken basis becomes explicit. The Hermit in energy encourages considering how the misunderstanding arose and sharing that understanding. The Tower in emotions describes feeling shaken by lost certainty. The visible correction of a conversation differs here from experiencing the collapse of an earlier conclusion. You can already understand the new words without yet feeling comfortable about the mistake discovered.

For example, an argument about a sharp phrase reveals that you were discussing a quotation from a message thread, having taken it as the other person’s own opinion. The objection’s basis falls away. **A clear correction does not cancel the force of what was felt**. You explain how you read the message and what is understood now. The misunderstanding clears, but confidence in familiar ways of reading messages can waver. Calling the incident trivial immediately is unnecessary: an important distinction has emerged while the unexpected discovery still affects the conversation.

Difficulty grows if reassurance requires a complete guarantee that no future phrase will allow misreading. Understanding then gives way to unattainable infallibility. Constructive Hermit energy helps separate this particular understood mistake from uncertainty about future exchanges. You can explain the present meaning seriously without promising to eliminate every misunderstanding; feeling shaken has room without becoming grounds to demand impossible clarity from every later message.
